lines.japanese: 教室の扉を開けたら、いくつかの目が集まってきた。
lines.english: When I opened the classroom door, several pairs of eyes turned toward me.

lines.japanese: だけど、こっそり無音で挨拶してくれた渡来さん以外の視線は、すぐにそれぞれ元の位置へ戻る。
lines.english: But except for Watarai, who greeted me secretly and without a sound, every gaze soon returned to its former place.

lines.japanese: 窓を開けられない地上６階の教室は、天井から吐きだされる温風がこもって、今日も息苦しかった。
lines.english: The windows in our sixth-floor classroom could not be opened. Warm air pouring from the ceiling gathered inside, and once again the room was stifling.

lines.japanese: 僕は列なす机のあぜ道を進んで、窓際の後ろから三番目の席に自分の鞄を置いた。
lines.english: I followed the narrow path between rows of desks and set my bag at the third seat from the back beside the windows.

lines.japanese: それから……椅子は引かずにそのまま、さらに後ろへと向かう。
lines.english: Then… without pulling out my chair, I continued farther back.

lines.japanese: 針生さんの席はたしか、隣りの列のいちばん後ろ……ここだったと思う。
lines.english: Hariu’s seat was, if I remembered correctly, at the back of the next row… This should be it.

lines.japanese: ちょっと迷ってから、念のため机の中を覗かせてもらうことにした。
lines.english: After a moment’s hesitation, I decided to check inside the desk to make sure.

lines.japanese: しゃがみこんで椅子を引くと、ほとんどの教科のテキストやノートが押し寿司みたいにぎっしり詰まっていた。
lines.english: I crouched and pulled out the chair. Textbooks and notebooks for nearly every subject were packed inside like pressed sushi.

lines.japanese: いちばん上のキャンパスノートを引っこぬくと、大人みたいな崩し字で小さく彼の苗字が書いてあった。針生さんの席に間違いないと確認できたので、僕は託された鞄を机の脇に提げた。
lines.english: I drew out the notebook on top. His surname was written there in small, flowing script, like an adult’s handwriting. Certain now that this was Hariu’s desk, I hung the bag entrusted to me from its side.

lines.japanese: 立ちあがると、近くの席に集まっていた女子たち六つの目が、僕を不思議そうに観察していた。
lines.english: When I stood, the six puzzled eyes of three girls gathered around the nearby desks were studying me.

lines.japanese: 「なんで羽田がハリウッドの鞄持ってんの」
lines.english: “Why is Haneda carrying Hollywood’s bag?”

lines.japanese: 女子の学級委員を務める高内さんが、職務質問する警官みたいな口調で尋ねてきた。
lines.english: Takauchi, the girls’ class representative, questioned me like a police officer making a street stop.

lines.japanese: 「頼まれたから……さっき駅で会って……」
lines.english: “He asked me to… I ran into him at the station…”

lines.japanese: 高内さんはすぐに大きな声を出すので、僕は彼女と話すのが苦手だった。注意していないとつい目線が泳いでしまう。
lines.english: Takauchi was quick to raise her voice, so I found her difficult to talk to. Unless I took care, my eyes began wandering of their own accord.

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。知らなかった。あんた、あのおっさんと仲いいんだ？」
lines.english: “Huh. Never knew you were friends with that old man.”

lines.japanese: 「どうかな……そうでもないんだけど……」
lines.english: “I’m not sure… I wouldn’t say we were…”

lines.japanese: 針生さんの机に目を落としながら答えた。天板の隅に、僕には読めない五線譜の落書きがあった。
lines.english: I answered with my eyes on Hariu’s desk. In one corner of the desktop, someone had scribbled music I could not read.

lines.japanese: 高内さんたちのひそひそ囁きあう声が耳に触れる。パシリとかシモベとか言ってるみたいだった。
lines.english: The girls’ whispers brushed my ears. I thought I heard lackey and servant among them.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、ちょうどいーわ」
lines.english: “Well, perfect timing.”

lines.japanese: 囁きから一転、はっきりした声が僕に突きつけられた。
lines.english: The whispering ceased, and a clear voice was thrust at me.

lines.japanese: 「さっき担任に言われたんだけどぉー。あのおっさん、残りの授業バックレる気まんまんらしいから、学級委員が説得しとけだってー。よろー」
lines.english: “Our homeroom teacher just told me that old man’s apparently planning to ditch every class we have left, so the class reps have to talk him out of it. Have fun.”

lines.japanese: 高内さんは──３年Ａ組の副委員長は「学級委員」という言葉をまるで他人事のように使った。
lines.english: Takauchi—the deputy representative of Class 3-A—used the words “class reps” as though they had nothing to do with her.

lines.japanese: 「いや……無理だよ、おれには」
lines.english: “No… I can’t do that.”

lines.japanese: そんなこと頼まれても困る。ついさっき、きっぱり拒絶されてしまった年下の子供に、いったいどうしたら彼を言いくるめられるんだろう。
lines.english: I could hardly accept such an assignment. How was a child younger than him, whom he had flatly rejected only minutes ago, supposed to talk him into anything?

lines.japanese: しかし高内さんは、何も知らないのに「ダイジョブ、ダイジョブ」と大口を開けて言いきる。
lines.english: But Takauchi, knowing nothing, opened her mouth wide and declared, “You’ll be fine, you’ll be fine.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あとアレ。担任がそろそろ準備、あのホラ、卒業文集？　アレ作る準備しとけッつってた。まず学級会議やって、役割分担だ何だいろいろ決めてくンだって」
lines.english: “Oh, and the other thing. Our teacher says it’s about time to start getting ready for… You know, the graduation anthology? First we’re supposed to hold a class meeting and decide who’s doing what and all that.”
“Right…”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあテストも終わるし……ちょっと今日の放課後、ふたりで概要決めとこうか……」
lines.english: “Then, since exams finish today… why don’t the two of us work out the broad plan after school?”

lines.japanese: 「今日の放課後、ふたりで概要決めとこうか……」
lines.english: “Why don’t the two of us work out the broad plan after school…”

lines.japanese: 高内さんが暗く沈んだ声でぼそぼそ繰りかえした。どうやら僕の物真似らしい。彼女の友人たちが手を叩いて笑っていた。
lines.english: Takauchi repeated it in a low, gloomy mumble. Apparently she was imitating me. Her friends clapped and laughed.

lines.japanese: 高内さんは片方の眉を吊りあげて、笑顔らしきものを作った。
lines.english: Takauchi raised one eyebrow and fashioned something resembling a smile.

lines.japanese: 「エ、なにそれ。あんた、私に気でもあんの？」
lines.english: “What’s that supposed to mean? Do you have a thing for me?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、良くないでしょー、若い男女が教室にふたりっきりで残ってさー。あ、なに？　私、明日香さまの代わり？」
lines.english: “A young man and woman staying all alone together in the classroom? That doesn’t sound very wholesome. What, am I your substitute for Lady Asuka?”

lines.japanese: 「なに言ってんだよ、そういうことじゃなくて……」
lines.english: “What are you talking about? That has nothing to do with it…”

lines.japanese: 「じゃー、ひとりでやってよ」
lines.english: “Then do it yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでおれが……高内さんだって学級委員だろ……」
lines.english: “Why should I…? You’re a class representative too.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ。したら私、アレやるよ。学級会議の板書とか、あとなんだ、買い出し？」
lines.english: “Fine. Then I’ll do the, you know, writing on the board during the meeting. And what else? Buying supplies?”

lines.japanese: 彼女の友人たちが、僕の代弁をするように「あんた楽なのばっかじゃんソレ」とか言って冷やかしてたけど、高内さんはただ甲高い声をあげて笑うだけだった。
lines.english: Her friends teased her—“You picked all the easy jobs”—as though speaking for me, but Takauchi merely laughed in a shrill voice.

lines.japanese: 僕は唇を結ばず、下を向いたり窓の外を眺めたりしながら、反撃の糸口を探した。
lines.english: I stood there with my mouth half-open, looking down and then out the window as I searched for some opening through which to strike back.

lines.japanese: でも、すでに友人たちとテストの問題予想に話題を移している彼女には、何を言ったところで軽くひと薙ぎされて終わる気がした。
lines.english: But she had already turned to predicting exam questions with her friends, and I felt that anything I said would be swept aside with a flick of her hand.

lines.japanese: テスト直前の貴重な時間を、こんなところで無駄に費やすわけにもいかない。僕はそう思うことにして、すごすごと自分の席へ戻った。
lines.english: I could hardly waste these precious minutes before the exam here. Having decided to see it that way, I slunk back to my own seat.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: 自分の席に着くと、教科書を開きもしないうちに予鈴が鳴った。
lines.english: No sooner had I sat down than the warning bell rang, before I could even open my textbook.

lines.japanese: なかなか頭に入らない教科書を五分ばかり眺めているうち、やがて本鈴が鳴り、担任の恩田先生が入ってきた。
lines.english: I spent about five minutes staring at the textbook without absorbing much. Then the class bell rang and our homeroom teacher, Ms. Onda, entered.

lines.japanese: キャリア３年という若さのわりに生気の薄い女性教師は、淡々とクラス名簿を読みあげて、淡々と出欠状況を確認する。
lines.english: For a teacher only three years into her career, she possessed remarkably little vitality. In a flat voice she read the class roll, and in a flat voice confirmed attendance.

lines.japanese: 名前を呼ばれても返答のない生徒がふたりいた。
lines.english: Two names received no answer.

lines.japanese: 針生蔵人。
lines.english: Kurodo Hariu.

lines.japanese: 山科京。
lines.english: Miyako Yamashina.

lines.japanese: 返事がなかったとき、恩田先生はいずれも慣れた手つきで事務的に斜線を引いただけだった。
lines.english: Each time silence answered, Ms. Onda simply drew a practiced, businesslike slash.

lines.japanese: 僕はふたつ前の空席を見る。持ち主不在の窓際の机には、ガラス越しの白い景観がよく似合っていた。思いだしてみれば、その机の主は──山科さんは、最近そこに座っていないことが多かった。
lines.english: I looked at the empty seat two places ahead. The unoccupied desk by the window suited the white landscape beyond the glass. Now that I thought of it, its owner—Yamashina—had often been absent lately.

lines.japanese: 詳しいことは知らないけど、病気がちなのだと聞いている。それでも成績のいい彼女のこと、もしかしたらもう推薦入学が決まって、残りの学園生活は消化試合なのかもしれない。
lines.english: I knew no details, only that she was frequently ill. Then again, her grades were excellent. Perhaps she had already secured a university place by recommendation and was merely playing out the rest of her school days.

lines.japanese: それから僕は、横目で斜め後ろを窺う。持ち主不在の方がかえって違和感のない、針生さんの机。
lines.english: Then I glanced back and to the side. Hariu’s desk looked, if anything, more natural without its owner.

lines.japanese: ふと、校門で耳にしたあの噂がよみがえる。
lines.english: The rumor I had heard by the school gates suddenly returned to me.

lines.japanese: “今日ガッコ休んでるヤツいたらソイツとか、ちょー、怪しンじゃね？”
lines.english: “If anyone’s off school today, that’d be super suspicious, right?”

lines.japanese: 朝のテレビ画面に映った柳木原の繁華街。少年たちの乱闘事件。怪我をしていた素行不良の同級生。
lines.english: Yanagihara’s entertainment district on the morning news. A brawl between boys. A delinquent classmate who was injured.

lines.japanese: 僕は教壇に目を戻した。知恵熱でも出たみたいに頭が重かった。
lines.english: I turned my eyes back to the lectern. My head felt heavy, as though thought itself had given me a fever.

lines.japanese: 朝のショートホームルームが終わると、僕らは選択授業ごとに並びなおした。ほどなく担当教諭がやってきて、そして期末考査の最終日が始まった。
lines.english: When the short morning homeroom ended, we rearranged ourselves according to our elective subjects. Before long the teacher in charge arrived, and the last day of final exams began.

lines.japanese: 世界史はそこそこ得意だったつもりだけど、今日はなんだかみんなのシャーペンの音がうるさくて、いまひとつ集中できなかった。
lines.english: I had always considered world history one of my better subjects. Today, however, everyone’s mechanical pencils seemed unbearably loud, and I could not quite concentrate.

lines.japanese: そう、それだ。
lines.english: Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: テスト用紙が回収されると、教官が退室するのも待てず、クラス中が一斉に騒ぎだす。
lines.english: The instant our papers were collected, the whole class erupted without even waiting for the proctor to leave.

lines.japanese: 五日間に渡った期末試験が、残すところあと一科目で終わろうとしている。根強く残った緊張感と、じわじわ押しよせてくる解放感が、教室に低いどよめきを湧きたたせていた。
lines.english: Five days of final exams stood one subject away from ending. The last stubborn tension and a gathering sense of freedom stirred a low rumble through the classroom.

lines.japanese: 放課後のプランを練る浮かれた声があちこちから聞こえる。ラーメン、カラオケ、ゲームセンター。
lines.english: Excited voices planned the afternoon on every side. Ramen. Karaoke. The arcade.

lines.japanese: 僕はひとり、苦手な数学のテキストに没頭──
lines.english: Alone, I immersed myself in my textbook for math, a subject I struggled with—

lines.japanese: ──しようとした。ところが。
lines.english: —or attempted to. However…

lines.japanese: 「羽田君」
lines.english: “Haneda.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 頭を上げると、渡来さんがあのきりっとした格好いい笑顔で僕の目の前に立っていた。
lines.english: I looked up. Watarai stood before me wearing that handsome, self-assured smile.

lines.japanese: 「きのう教えてもらったおかげで、世界史ばっちりだった。ありがとう」
lines.english: “Thanks to what you taught me yesterday, world history went perfectly. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: ぴっ。おなかの横で地味なＶサイン。
lines.english: She flashed a modest V-sign beside her waist.

lines.japanese: 「あ……そうなんだ……よかった」
lines.english: “Oh… Really…? I’m glad.”

lines.japanese: 僕は戸惑いながら答えた。いままでに彼女が、みんなのいる前で僕に話しかけてきたことはあまりない。近くにいた男子たちが、目配せしながら何かささやき合っていた。
lines.english: I answered in confusion. She had seldom spoken to me in front of everyone before. Several boys nearby exchanged looks and began whispering.

lines.japanese: 彼女はその空気に気付いたようだった。尾行を気にする知能犯みたいにちらりと瞳を泳がせ、呆れたように小さな息をついた。
lines.english: She seemed to notice the atmosphere. Her eyes flicked about like a clever criminal checking for a tail, and she let out a small, exasperated breath.

lines.japanese: 「うざ」
lines.english: “Annoying.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでもない。それじゃ最後の一コ、がんばろうね」
lines.english: “Nothing. Well, let’s do our best on the last one.”

lines.japanese: それだけ言って、渡来さんは通りすぎるように去っていった。
lines.english: With only that, Watarai left as though merely passing by.

lines.japanese: なんだろう。
lines.english: What was it?

lines.japanese: なんだか……なんだろう。疑問が疑問にすらならない。僕は気になる女の子から声をかけられても、その喜び方すら忘れてしまったみたいだ。
lines.english: Somehow… What was it? The question could not even become a question. It seemed I had forgotten how to feel happy when a girl I was interested in spoke to me.

lines.japanese: ぼーっとしていたら、クラスでいちばん頭のいい男子グループと目が合ってしまったので、僕はなんとなく席を立った。
lines.english: While I sat there dazed, my eyes met those of the smartest group of boys in the class. For no particular reason, I rose from my seat.

lines.japanese: そして……なんとなく教室を出た。たぶん、視線を振りはらいたかったんだと思う。
lines.english: Then… for no particular reason, I left the room. I think I wanted to shake off their eyes.

lines.japanese: でも行くところなんてない。こんなときは、森里君にあの遠慮のない声で「おまえマジでアホだな！」なんて、気安く頭をはたいてもらいたかった。
lines.english: But I had nowhere to go. At a time like this, I wanted Morisato to smack me casually on the head and say, in that voice of his which never held anything back, “You really are an idiot.”

lines.japanese: 森里君。僕のたったひとりの友達。
lines.english: Morisato. My one and only friend.

lines.japanese: だけど、こっそり覗きに行ったＨ組の教室に、彼の姿はなかった。
lines.english: But when I stole a look into the Class H classroom, he was not there.

lines.japanese: またあのくだらない噂話が思いだされる。
lines.english: That ridiculous rumor returned to me once more.

lines.japanese: “いるとすりゃ９０％セントヘレナのヤツだし。”
lines.english: “If we do, there’s a ninety-percent chance he’s from Saint Helena.”

lines.japanese: 僕はもう一度、Ｈ組教室の戸枠に張りついて念入りに目を凝らす。
lines.english: I clung to the Class H doorframe and peered inside again, searching carefully.

lines.japanese: 真面目な生徒が多い美空学園の中でも、とりわけ茶色や金色に華やいだ頭が多い３年Ｈ組。またの名を特別強化学級。
lines.english: At Misora Academy, where most students were studious, Class 3-H stood out for its profusion of heads bright with brown and gold. Its other name was the special remedial class.

lines.japanese: 森里君の所属するクラスは、まさしく一部の心ない生徒から流刑島と呼ばれているそこだった。
lines.english: Morisato belonged to the very class that a few unkind students called the island of exile.

lines.japanese: 頭が重い。
lines.english: My head felt heavy.

lines.japanese: みんなどこに行ってしまったんだろう。僕はただ、誰でもいい誰かと他愛のない歓談がしたいだけなのに。
lines.english: Where had everyone gone? All I wanted was to exchange a few idle words with someone—anyone.

lines.japanese: 僕はさっさと教室に戻った。数学の試験が始まるまで何も考えず、ただひとり教科書に目を通していた。
lines.english: I hurried back to my classroom. Until the math exam began, I tried to think of nothing at all and read my textbook alone.
